S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

patient_info.stressor: After a paddleboarding accident left Edward with a deep leg wound that required repeated medical follow-up, his usual preference for planning and cleanliness became tied to a sharper sense that small oversights could have serious consequences. As he returned to engineering work, intrusive unwanted doubts began attaching themselves to both his recovery routines and his CAD deliverables, and he increasingly relied on repeated checking and other fixed routines to feel able to move on. Over time, the pattern began delaying project milestones, stretching his workdays, and disrupting the outdoor schedule he normally used to stay balanced. He eventually contacted a psychiatrist through his employer’s health plan after realizing that better spreadsheets and stricter routines were no longer containing the problem.

S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.
S065.manifestation: Even after I know I’ve cleaned the wound area or reviewed a CAD file, a thought keeps cutting in that I missed one tiny thing and it’s going to turn into an infection or a design mistake that hurts someone, and I can’t just reason it away.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: What brings me in is that I’m losing hours to rechecking things—my dressing supplies, door locks, file dimensions, revision notes—because I don’t feel allowed to move on until I’ve gone through the same routine enough times that the anxiety drops.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My project deadlines have started slipping because I stay late trying to get comfortable enough to submit work, and I’ve stopped making it to paddleboarding meetups or workouts because the routines eat up the time I used to keep for myself.
